atoms.text: This is Edgar the Eagle, he is going to teach you about the physical geography of some hills.

instruction.text: These are the South Downs in Sussex. Find the hills to learn more.

feedback.end: A hill is an area of land that rises higher than its surroundings. They are smaller and less steep than mountains. The tops of hills can join up to form a ridge line.

instruction.text: Now we are in the Yorkshire Dales. Find the footpath to learn more.

feedback.end: The Yorkshire Dales are an area of hills in the North of England. A dale is another word for a valley. Valleys are the lower areas in between mountains and hills.

instruction.text: Edgar would like to visit the US to make some observations about different hills. Answer Edgar’s questions.

atoms.a: “What do you notice about this hill?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m10'>What do you notice about this hill</voice>

feedback.correct: This is Monument Valley in the United States. The hill here is known as a butte. Buttes stand alone and have steep sides and flat tops. We do not have hills like this in the UK.

atoms.a: “What could we use to keep a record of our observations?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m10'>What could we use to keep a record of our observations</voice>

correct.text: Great! We can use the camera to take photos and then compare them to hills in the UK.

feedback.wrong: A bike might help us to get there, but it isn’t very useful for recording our observations.

instruction.text: We’re back on the South Downs. Select the closest sheep to learn more.

text: Most of the hills in the UK were once covered with forests, but the trees were cut down to make space for farm animals. Other animals, like this clouded yellow butterfly, have then adapted to the new environment.

atoms.a: A hill is steeper and taller than a mountain.
Valleys are the low areas in between hills and mountains.
A ridge line is the line along the top of a group of hills.
Humans have cut down the forests on many UK hills to keep farm animals.
